paper_metadata.title: A QUANTUM ALGORITHM FOR LINEAR PDES ARISING IN FINANCE

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid variational quantum imaginary‑time evolution algorithm to solve PDEs arising in option pricing by mapping the Black–Scholes equation to a Schrödinger equation. Numerical simulations use a 4‑qubit ansatz with 25 variational parameters (16 spatial grid points) and ~500 time steps to reconstruct European and Asian option prices with small errors compared to classical PDE solutions. All results are produced via classical simulation of the quantum circuit.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical imaginary-time-evolution experiment for pricing a European call option in the Black-Scholes model using a 4-qubit shallow ansatz circuit.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum imaginary time evolution (McLachlan principle) with a shallow Ry/H/X ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: 4-qubit layered ansatz with X, H, single-qubit Ry rotations, and controlled-Ry gates
algorithm.optimizer: numpy.linalg.lstsq for solving the linear system; Differential Evolution for initial ansatz fitting
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate in time until maturity; ansatz depth increased until initial-state approximation error <= epsilon_max
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial parameters theta_0 obtained by minimizing |||phi(theta)> - |psi(0)>||; optimization may use Differential Evolution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option price discretized on a 1D spatial grid with 4 qubits representing 16 points; quantum state amplitudes encode the discretized payoff/solution
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the imaginary-time Schrödinger equation equivalent to the Black-Scholes PDE for a European call option
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization via gamma(tau); boundary values imposed through discretization at xmin and xmax
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = (1/2) d^2/dx^2 discretized by second-order finite differences

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under Black-Scholes

dataset_specification.description: S0=K=100, T=1, sigma=20%, r=0, spatial grid [xmin,xmax] approx [3.9,5] corresponding to [50,150] in S

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Change of variables s=exp(x), tau=sigma^2(T-t); finite-difference discretization on equidistant grid; normalization of payoff state
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare quantum ansatz evolution against classical simulation; report state-vector error and price curves

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference discretization of the PDE; ansatz fitting to initial payoff state
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover option price in original coordinates using known scaling parameter gamma(tau)

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents a near-term hybrid algorithm and numerical accuracy results only; no asymptotic or empirical speedup is claimed.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed in the paper; current demonstration uses a 4‑qubit discretization (16 grid points) and 25 variational parameters.
limiting_factors: Only 4 qubits (16 spatial grid points) used for PDE discretization
Results produced via classical numerical simulation of the algorithm rather than execution on quantum hardware
No asymptotic complexity comparison with classical PDE solvers
Classical preprocessing and parameter updates dominate the hybrid workflow

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper describes a proposed hybrid algorithm and numerical simulations, but no specific QPU/device is named.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; 25 Ry gates are reported, so gate count is used as a proxy for circuit size, not depth.
